AlternateTargets: the lacquer bucket is not sharp

ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: A dull lacquer bucket combines a black, closed container with the judgment “not quick” or “not sharp.” Chan masters use it as a blunt rebuke or answer when someone fails to see, asks after conceptual formulas, or cannot sort the matter placed before him.
EvidenceBody: Dahui Zonggao answers a question about the four elements with the phrase.
Sanyi Yu stops an endless patriarchal count, throws down the staff, and calls the addressee a dull lacquer bucket.
Langting Ting gives exactly the same reply to three consecutive conceptual questions from a layman.
Miyun Yuanwu says the unresolved assembly leaves him with no remedy for the dull lacquer bucket.
Wanshou Huisu gives it after an interlocutor admits he does not understand.
Juelang Daosheng contrasts excessive naturalness with the dull lacquer bucket and excessive confusion with a wild fox.

Senses.Note: One hundred nine exact hits occur in sixty-seven frozen works. Seven witnesses preserve direct answer, repeated answer, rebuke, contrast, and assembly address.
